criticalAcademicFindings: Programming and network/OS study are real foundations, not security doctrine by title.
Cyber Attacks explicitly teaches buffer overflow, injection, DDoS and malware vulnerabilities/attacks; Defence teaches security controls, depth/breadth and organizational security-program design.

Offenders applies criminological explanations to hacking, illicit platforms, hybrid online/offline crime and criminal networks. Victims teaches actual victimology, online risks, repeated victimization, impacts and legal status.

Criminal Law applies doctrine to hacking, malware, digital offences and real operations; Criminal Investigation teaches digital evidence, investigative powers, jurisdiction/anonymity/encryption and rights-based case analysis.

Governance/Organizations and Crisis Management teach cyber-risk identification, human factors, security culture, controls, incident lifecycle and public/private response; Cyberconflict teaches statecraft, operations and diplomacy.

The 10-EC online-deception project and 10-EC ransomware integration are substantive taught inquiry, not merely possible student topics. Ransomware requires an integrated technical, crime, law and governance analysis and acute-response advice.
boundary: All 23 supported components total 150 EC: first 120 required plus genuine 30 open. Remaining 30 required EC, final-work individual weight/access/assessment and full degree progression are excluded. No invented thesis, weights, routes, open-space contents or future offerings.
